market_holds: Spot $18.79 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-12 18:09 UTC). Front-expiry (11-20) straddle 25.9%, event-implied move 24.7%, ATM spread 63% of mid so indicative only; put/call OI 0.4. Run-up +9.6% over 5 sessions, +10.9% over 20; in my own Yahoo bars the stock went from $14.04 (11-02) to $18.77 (+34%) in 8 sessions, in step with AppLovin ($228.85 to $400, +75%) and Unity ($38.87 to $50.36, +30%) after their Q3 prints on 11-04 and 11-05. StockStory ties the 11-05 +9.4% day directly to those peer prints. Only one prior public print: 2026-08-12 amc, -20.6% on a beat (rev $219.5m vs ~$208m consensus) because the Q3 guide ($217-222m) was flat sequentially after +7% q/q; per a Benzinga-sourced snippet that guide was still above the ~$214.8m consensus at the time, and the FY guide of $870-880m was above ~$856m. Consensus for Q3 as of 2026-11-04 (Earnings Whispers): revenue ~$220.9m, EPS $0.17, whisper $0.20. That is essentially the guide midpoint and was set before the peer prints; I found no dated revision after them. The FY guide implies Q4 of about $231m (+5% q/q), my arithmetic below. Short interest about 0.4% of float (MarketBeat, undated), so this is not a crowded short. IPO at $23 on 2026-06-04, so the stock is still below issue and 34% under its 52-week high. The 180-day lock-up ends about 2026-11-30/12-01 (Wedbush via Finimize; an IPO tracker), with Blackstone and General Atlantic as likely sellers.
view: The line this stock trades on is the sequential revenue shape: the Q3 number against a flat guide, and above all the Q4 guide and FY raise. That is what sank it in August. The ecosystem since the company last spoke points to a beat. AppLovin's Q3 was +14% q/q, about $100m over the top of its guide, with gaming ads up nearly 50% y/y, and it guided Q4 +8-10% q/q. Unity's Vector grew 40% q/q against a 20% guide, and Unity guided strategic Grow up about 20% q/q for Q4. Prediction markets, which Wedbush names as one of Liftoff's non-gaming drivers, spent hard into the NFL season: kickoff-week downloads were Polymarket ~0.76-1.2m and Kalshi ~0.6-0.9m, and football contract volume ran about 4x a year earlier. Liftoff's Q3 guide of 0-1% q/q looks conservative next to that, against last year's roughly +10% Q2-to-Q3 seasonal step. This is an IPO-year sponsor-owned company that beat consensus by 5.5% in its first print, and it has a lock-up ending about 18 days after this release. So a revenue beat above $222m is more likely than not, perhaps 70-75%. Whether that makes the stock go up is far less clear. First, the stock already took a third of a move up on the peers alone, and its own news was not part of that. Second, the bar has been raised to something like a beat-and-raise in line with peers, while the stale $221m consensus does not show it. Third, the August print showed this tape punishes a beat that comes with a soft sequential guide. Fourth, the obvious bear reading of the peer prints is share loss: AppLovin's Axon and Unity's Vector take ROAS-driven gaming budgets from mid-tier DSPs, and Liftoff's guided 21-24% y/y next to peers at 50-126% fits that story. A Q4 guide around +5% q/q could read as a share loser next to Unity's +20% and AppLovin's +9%. I lean modestly up and not enough to bet.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the Q3 revenue beat. The $220.9m consensus dates from before the AppLovin and Unity prints and sits at the guide midpoint, and the ecosystem data since then (peer beats, the prediction-market NFL push) point above it. But the price has moved about 34% with those same peers, so the market has plausibly re-marked the whisper even though the published consensus has not changed. I cannot show the beat is unpriced, so I don't claim it.

recommendation.reason: Peer and vertical data since August make a Q3 revenue beat likely, and the published consensus is stale. But the stock's run-in came with the peers' prints, not its own news. The only prior reaction punished a beat for a soft sequential guide, and the peer prints can be read as share gains at Liftoff's expense. That leaves the direction near 56%, well short of the 65% the playbook requires.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The Q4 revenue guide. Implied Q4 well above $240m (a FY raise to roughly $900m+), or a disclosed non-gaming acceleration, would make it a clear up. A Q4 guide near the $231m the FY range already implies, or commentary about losing gaming share, would make it a clear down.

self_critique: The case for up is stronger than 56 if the peers show a rising tide rather than share shift. Liftoff grew 35% alongside AppLovin and Unity in Q2, the guide is IPO-year conservative, and sponsors facing a lock-up have every reason to beat and raise. The stock still sits below its IPO price and 25% below its pre-August level, so even a raise to the peers' standard has room to run. The case for down is just as concrete: the identical setup in August (beat, guide above consensus) produced -20%, the stock has just added a third on someone else's news, and AppLovin's and Unity's model-driven acceleration is exactly what takes ROAS budgets from a mid-tier DSP. Neither side clears 65.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition did the most work here: it showed the 34% run-up was peer beta, which cancelled the beat lean from the peer data. P7's call to estimate the deciding line from counterparties helped frame the Q4 guide arithmetic, but peers that are competitors cut both ways (rising tide or share take), and the playbook does not say how to read that.
